answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. Votes are weighted by stake, and a challenge window lets anyone submit evidence that several identities share an operator; if adjudicators confirm coordinated, deceptive voting, those identities lose their deposits. This does not make Sybils impossible, but makes influence costly: an attacker must acquire and risk capital for every fake account, while a dawn-time echo of copied credentials gains no weight without its own cipher-backed stake.
